reason: The text explicitly demonstrates Yahweh's goal to help the Hebrew people through multiple affirmations: (1) God's direct statement to Jacob: 'I will do you good' (וְאֵיטִ֥יבָה עִמָּֽךְ, 32:12), (2) the covenant promise to make his offspring as numerous as the sand of the sea (32:12), (3) God's blessing of Jacob during the wrestling encounter at Jabbok (32:29), and (4) the renaming of Jacob to Israel, signifying his elevated status as ancestor of God's chosen people. The entire narrative demonstrates God's active involvement in protecting, guiding, and blessing Jacob, who becomes the patriarch of the Hebrew people.
